Kulashi Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kulashi, Georgia

Not demolished. Kulashi, first documented in the 16th century, was historically majority-Jewish, with residents arriving over centuries from Akhaltsikhe, Lailashi, Bandza, Sujuna, and Racha. German traveler Johann Anton Güldenstädt noted the community in the 1770s; the 1870s Tbilisi-Poti railway further boosted local trade. The village had four synagogues, the oldest a wooden structure from 1862, with about 300 Jews recorded in 1916. Kulashi became notably active in the Soviet-era aliyah struggle - after Israel-bound emigration was banned in 1969, 18 families petitioned the UN Commission on Human Rights for repatriation, and most of Kulashi's Jews left for Israel by the 1970s. This cemetery, opposite the village's synagogues, holds tombstones from 1872 to 2011.
